newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson shares climb on sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Thomson shares climb on sale plans.

text.p: Shares in French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF climbed on Wednesday after the government announced it planned to privatise the company through a private placement.
At 1130 GMT Thomson shares were up 4.56 percent at 183.5 francs, the highest level this year. The CAC-40 index of leading shares was down 0.05 percent.
Traders said the government's decision to sell the company by private placement, accompanied by a book of terms and conditions, rather than a public offering should lead to a better share valuation.
"The privatisation will go ahead through a private placement, quickly, and, no doubt, at a better price than through a public offering, a fund manager said.
"A public offering would have scattered the capital, whereas here, they are selling control of the company and that has a cost," he said.
However, the prospect of a good valuation of Thomson's shares weighed on likely candidates for the purchase of the defence electronics group.
Alcatel Alsthom was down 1.02 percent at 583 francs after touching a low of 578 francs earlier while Lagardere fell 2.99 percent to 162 francs.
Traders also said Thomson shares were benefiting simply from the fact there had been an announcement.
"The government has finally given its opinion and traders are reassessing the project," a trader said.
